resources.title: Attached
resources.author: Amir Levine & Rachel Heller
resources.description: The definitive guide to adult attachment theory. Explains anxious, avoidant, and secure styles in plain language and why we are drawn to people who feel familiar, not safe.

resources.title: The Body Keeps the Score
resources.author: Bessel van der Kolk
resources.description: A landmark book on how trauma shapes the body and mind — and the range of approaches that can help. Particularly relevant if the relationship involved emotional or psychological abuse.

resources.title: We Can Do Hard Things
resources.author: Glennon Doyle
resources.description: Honest, warm conversations about difficult human experiences. Not specifically about breakups, but consistently useful for anyone going through something hard.

resources.title: Psychology Today Therapist Finder
resources.description: International directory of licensed therapists, searchable by issue, therapy type, and location. A practical starting point if you are considering professional support.

resources.title: Why Does He Do That?
resources.author: Lundy Bancroft
resources.description: A clear-eyed look at controlling and abusive relationship dynamics — written for people who are still trying to understand what happened. Widely recommended by therapists.

resources.title: Getting Past Your Breakup
resources.author: Susan J. Elliott
resources.description: A practical, structured guide to breakup recovery grounded in cognitive-behavioural principles. More hands-on than most self-help books on the topic — exercises included.

resources.title: Relationship Alive
resources.author: Neil Sattin
resources.description: In-depth interviews with leading researchers and therapists on attachment, intimacy, and relationships. Useful for understanding what went wrong and what healthy looks like.

resources.title: Running on Empty
resources.author: Jonice Webb
resources.description: On childhood emotional neglect — the invisible wound that often shapes who we are drawn to in relationships. Quietly illuminating for many people in or after difficult relationships.

resources.title: The Holistic Psychologist
resources.author: Dr Nicole LePera
resources.description: Accessible content on self-healing, nervous system regulation, and breaking relational patterns. Instagram and website both useful; start with the self-healing protocol.

resources.title: The Science of Healing Heartbreak
resources.author: We Can Do Hard Things
resources.description: Florence Williams on the neuroscience and biology of heartbreak — why it feels physical, what your body and brain are actually going through, and what helps. One of the most clarifying listens for early days.

resources.title: Baggage Reclaim
resources.author: Natalie Lue
resources.description: One of the most practical and honest resources on no-contact, boundaries, and breaking patterns in relationships. Articles, podcast, and exercises specifically aimed at people recovering from difficult relationships.

resources.title: Self-Compassion
resources.author: Dr Kristin Neff
resources.description: Free guided meditations, exercises, and research-backed tools for self-compassion. Particularly useful when shame or self-blame is part of what you are carrying. Start with the self-compassion break.

resources.title: How to Fix a Broken Heart
resources.author: TED — Guy Winch
resources.description: A 12-minute TED talk on why heartbreak is a genuine psychological injury, why we treat it so poorly, and what actually helps. The best short introduction to taking your own pain seriously.

resources.title: Whole Again
resources.author: Jackson MacKenzie
resources.description: A compassionate guide to healing after a relationship with a toxic or emotionally unavailable partner. Goes beyond the relationship itself to the patterns that led you there.

resources.title: Dr Ramani
resources.author: Dr Ramani Durvasula
resources.description: The most accessible resource on narcissistic and difficult relationship dynamics. YouTube channel and website with hundreds of short, clear videos. Particularly useful if you are still trying to make sense of what happened.

resources.title: Unlocking Us
resources.author: Brené Brown
resources.description: Brené Brown in conversation with researchers, authors, and thinkers on vulnerability, shame, and what it means to live fully. Several episodes directly relevant to heartbreak and starting over.

resources.title: Codependent No More
resources.author: Melody Beattie
resources.description: The classic book on codependency — the pattern of losing yourself in another person's needs, emotions, and crises. Widely recommended for anyone whose relationship felt like it consumed their identity.

resources.title: The Gifts of Imperfection
resources.author: Brené Brown
resources.description: On letting go of who you think you should be and embracing who you are. Warm and research-grounded. A good companion for the part of healing where you start to rebuild your sense of self.

resources.title: Huberman Lab
resources.author: Andrew Huberman
resources.description: Science-based tools for improving wellbeing — sleep, stress, focus, and emotional regulation. Several episodes directly relevant to grief, nervous system recovery, and rebuilding after loss.

resources.title: When the Body Says No
resources.author: Gabor Maté
resources.description: How chronic stress and suppressed emotion — often rooted in difficult relationships — manifests in the body. A deeper read for understanding the physical toll of what you have been through.
